title: A version bump cannot prove its lockfile is current, because the bumped versions are not published yet
description:
FOUND THE HARD WAY during the 0.8.0 release, 2026-09-19. bun.lock still pinned @opum-ai/lore-*@0.7.0 in optionalDependencies after the bump to 0.8.0. Every CI job then failed at the setup-bun step with 'error: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen' -- on dev and on every open PR at once.

THE MECHANISM, which is the whole point of this task. At bump time the 0.8.0 platform packages did NOT EXIST on npm, so bun could not resolve them and left bun.lock alone; --frozen-lockfile compared two things that still agreed and passed. PUBLISHING made those versions resolvable, and the SAME UNCHANGED LOCKFILE became stale the instant the registry could answer. PR #180 (the bump) and #181 (the promotion) were genuinely green; the next PR was genuinely red with no source change between them. The defect was latent from the bump and ARMED BY THE PUBLISH.

WHY THE EXISTING GATES CANNOT CATCH IT. release.yml's 'assert release package versions + metadata are consistent' job compares the declared version across package.json, npm/*/package.json and the plugin manifest -- all FILES, all internally consistent, all correct. bun.lock is the one version site whose correctness depends on the REGISTRY, and a registry check necessarily fails before the publish for a version that is supposed not to exist yet. So the check that would have caught it cannot be run at the moment it would help. That is the interesting shape, not the missed line.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK, unproven, for whoever picks this up:
 - Regenerate bun.lock as a STEP OF THE BUMP rather than as an assertion about it -- run bun install (unfrozen) in the release branch and commit the result, so the lockfile is produced by the bump instead of being checked afterwards. Removes the judgement rather than documenting it.
 - Or assert the narrow invariant that does not need the registry: every @opum-ai/lore-* version in bun.lock equals package.json's version. Pure file comparison, catchable at bump time, and it is exactly what was violated.
The second is cheap and testable; the first is stronger. They are not exclusive.

CONTEXT: the bump commit's own message read 'EVERY VERSION SITE, NAMED INDIVIDUALLY, because a set that agrees in most places is the failure mode this bump has hit before', then enumerated seven sites and missed this one. The enumeration was of files someone thought to list, which is precisely the kind of completeness a machine check exists to replace.

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/check-lockfile-pins.mjs exits 0 on this repository (six pins compared, each against root package.json's optionalDependencies) and 1 when any @opum-ai/lore-* pin in bun.lock is missing, extra, or differently versioned, naming the package, both versions and the remedy.
The same script is the one call site in both workflows: ci.yml's package-set job runs it on every pull request and release.yml's verify-versions runs it at dispatch, neither gated nor neutered.

A missing or unparseable bun.lock is exit 1 (a finding about the tree, never a pass) and an unreadable root package.json is exit 2; the success line names how many pins were compared and at which version.
test/check-lockfile-pins.test.ts proves both directions in one suite: a fixture whose lockfile pin lags the manifest goes red for that reason, and the real repository tree goes green.
bun test, bun run lint, bun run typecheck, bun run check:packages, bun run check:lockfile and bun run lore check all pass on the branch head.

plan: 1. scripts/check-lockfile-pins.mjs — read root package.json and bun.lock (JSONC: strip trailing commas outside strings, then JSON.parse), compare the lockfile workspace optionalDependencies against the manifest pins in both directions (key set and value), and any @opum-ai/lore* entry under packages. Exit 0/1/2, --root <dir> for fixtures, remedy named in the failure line.
2. Wire it: package.json check:lockfile, one step in ci.yml package-set (rename that job to cover both assertions), one step in release.yml verify-versions.

3. test/check-lockfile-pins.test.ts: fixture acceptance, one rejection test per failure shape, could-not-evaluate cases, JSONC acceptance, and the wiring pins (package.json script + both workflow call sites + no neutering).
4. Mutation-test the suite: stale-pin fixture red, real tree green, in one run; confirm the red comes from the pin comparison and not an unrelated problem.
5. Docs: name the gate in the bump paragraph of docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md via lore.
6. Gates: bun test, lint, typecheck, check:packages, check:lockfile, lore check. Reviewer pass (scripts/ + release.yml). PR into dev, land on green, cite the run.
